value.rationale: Two classical excitable rules have known pointwise equal periods on bicliques and an earlier eight/four discrepancy on the highly symmetric Petersen graph. The canonical asymmetric 12-vertex Frucht graph, with no nonidentity spatial automorphisms, offers a natural structural test of whether such a discrepancy depends on symmetry. The exact 1496-configuration exceptional class proves it does not; the all-state eight-pair census quantifies this structural contrast, while crediting the earlier period type. This is a complete natural finite comparison, not a claim of the first eight/four mismatch or an arbitrary graph slice.
